Sixteen comments

Timmy Clifford’s

Urs, here’s the first tune in the last track on Solas’ CD “Solas.” As they go through the tune, John Williams tosses a few more triplets into the mix on accordion, but this setting is pretty much what they play the first go round.

↳ Posted by Will Harmon on April 21st, 2002.

Micho Russell’s

This tune is called Micho Russell’s on Niamh Ni Charra’s album From Both Sides.

↳ Posted by davedupplaw on July 15th, 2009.

A cool tune,

like one for

ever sprightly marching in
the ever so green leafy cool shade of
an ever lasting hot summer day!

↳ Posted by birlibirdie on June 25th, 2012.

Timmy Clifford’s, X:2

I got this version from the mandolin player Kayla MacLachlan, who got it from Marla Fibish.

Kayla plays this after I Ne’er Shall Ween Her (https://thesession.org/tunes/803) and before The Cook In The Kitchen (https://thesession.org/tunes/808):

https://thesession.org/members/1/sets/14724

↳ Posted by Jeremy on November 23rd, 2018.

Re: Timmy Clifford’s

Just an FYI:
Timmy Clifford was a box player from Kerry who emigrated to Chicago. I don’t know if he composed the namesake tune or brought it with him from Ireland.
I believe he now lives in Sweden.

↳ Posted by Paul Grajciar on May 24th, 2021.

Re: Timmy Clifford’s

Liz Carroll laid this tune on me in a Chicago lesson-visit in about 1983 or so .. and yes, called it Timmy Clifford’s, IIRC.
At the time she was playing a bunch of her other original tunes, so I got the impression (whether mistaken or not ;-?) – that SHE had written it.
She suggested it might be followed nicely by one of Bobby Casey’s reels, at
https://thesession.org/tunes/270#setting39255
